subject: christian-religious-education
general_outcomes: Demonstrate an awareness of the love of God as the Sole Creator and heavenly father.
Acquire Christian values and morals to make informed day to day choices.
Recognize the Church as a house of God and participate in church activities to foster responsibility.
Utilise social media platforms appropriately as guided by Christian moral values and principles.
Apply the teachings of Jesus Christ in their interaction with others to form harmonious relationships.
Appreciate the Holy Bible as the word of God and apply its teachings in their day-to-day lives.

substrands.name: Holiness 4 lessons
learning_outcomes: describe ways of glorifying God with their bodies
acquire the value of holiness by keeping away from situations that lead to sin
recite 1 Corinthians 6:19 on the body as the temple of the Holy Spirit
desire to lead holy lives free from sin.
learning_experiences: in pairs read 1 Corinthians 6:19-20 and mention the lessons learnt
in pairs list sins that do not please God
in groups discuss how to avoid situations that lead to sin
sing a song on holiness.
inquiry_questions: Why should you lead holy lives as young people?
Question(s)
core_competencies: • Self-efficacy: the skill of knowing self is portrayed as learners discuss how to avoid situations that lead to sin.
pertinent_issues: • Social cohesion: learners discuss how to avoid situations that lead to sin.

substrands.name: House of God 2 lessons
learning_outcomes: outline lessons learnt from Matthew 21:12-14
participate in Church activities to grow spiritually
appreciate the Church as a house of worship.
learning_experiences: read Matthew 21:12-14 and list lessons learnt from the Bible text
read 1Corithinians 14:26 and list activities they do in church
in groups mention ways they serve God in Church
in pairs list ways of respecting the church as a house of God
write a poem about respecting the Church
sing a song related to serving God.
Suggested Learning Experiences
inquiry_questions: Why is the Church a holy place?
Key Inquiry Question(s)
core_competencies: • Collaboration: the skill of teamwork is portrayed as learners mention ways they serve God in Church.
values: • Responsibility is exhibited as learners list activities they should do in church.
pertinent_issues: • Social Cohesion: learners live harmoniously as they interact with each other.
links_to_other_areas: Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners sing sing a song related to serving God.
English: reading skills are enhanced as learners read the scriptures.

substrands.name: The Early Church 3 lessons
learning_outcomes: identify the first disciples of Jesus Christ from the scriptures provided
describe how the early church was started as outlined in Acts 2:38-41
desire to turn away from sins as stated in Acts 2:38.
learning_experiences: read Matthew 10:1-4 and list the disciples of Jesus Christ
sort the names of the 12 disciples by using flash cards
search for the names of the disciples in a word puzzle
watch a video clip on the twelve disciples
read Acts 2:38-41on how the early church was started
role play how the early church was started
repent their sins as guided in Acts 2:38.
Suggested Learning Experiences
inquiry_questions: How was the early church started?
Key Inquiry Question(s)
core_competencies: • Learning to learn: the skill of developing relationships is nurtured as learners carry out activities together such as sorting, searching and role playing.
values: Responsibility: learners learn how to take up their roles by following the example of the disciples of Jesus Christ. Links to other learning activity areas:
Mathematics: mathematical skills are applied as learners use flash cards to sort the names of the 12 disciples.
English: reading skills are enhanced as learners read the Holy Bible.
Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners engage in role play.
pertinent_issues: • Leadership: as they learn about the instructions given to the first disciples: Matthew 10:1-4.

substrands.name: Standing Firm in Faith 3 lessons
learning_outcomes: name the city where believers were first called Christians
retell how Stephen was stoned for standing firm in his faith
explain why they should not join ungodly groups
Utilize the virtue of assertiveness and stand firm in faith.
learning_experiences: sing a song related to standing firm in the Christian faith
read Acts 11: 26 and say where believers were first called Christians
identify Antioch, from a Bible map
in groups read Acts 7: 54-60 about how Stephen was stoned to death
list lessons learnt form the stoning of Stephen
explain why they should not join ungodly groups; radicalized groups, groups that do not recognise Jesus Christ
list ways they can stand firm in their Christian faith.
Suggested Learning Experiences
inquiry_questions: 1. Why should you stand firm in your Christian faith?
2. Why should you not join ungodly groups?
Key Inquiry
Question(s)
core_competencies: • Learning to learn: the skill of engaging in self-driven tasks is portrayed as learners identify Antioch from the map.
values: • Patriotism: learners explain why they should not join ungodly groups; radicalized groups and groups that do not recognize Jesus Christ.
pertinent_issues: Safety and Security: learners explain why they should not join ungodly groups; radicalized groups, groups that do not recognise Jesus Christ as their saviour.
Assertiveness: learners say No! to ungodly groups by standing firm in their faith.
links_to_other_areas: Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners sing songs.
English: reading skills are enhanced as learners read the scriptures.
Social Studies skills are applied as learners locate Antioch in the map.

substrands.name: The Lord’s Prayer 3 lessons
learning_outcomes: read Matthew 6:9-13 on the Lord’s prayer
recite the Lord’s prayer and pray always
say a prayer to God every day to grow spiritually.
learning_experiences: sing a song related to the Lord’s Prayer
read Matthew 6:9-13
discuss why it is important to pray everyday
pray for their parents/guardians, friends and relatives
recite the Lord’s prayer daily
list the number of times they pray and share with classmates.
inquiry_questions: Why should you pray always as a Christian?
core_competencies: • Collaboration: learners develop skill of teamwork as they discuss, sing and recite the Lord’s prayer.
values: • Unity is enhanced as learners pray for their parents/guardians, friends and relatives.
pertinent_issues: • Developmental perspective: self-Discipline is enhanced as learners recite the Lord’s prayer daily.
links_to_other_areas: Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners sing.
English: reading skills are enhanced as learners read the Bible.

substrands.name: Fruit of the Holy Spirit 3 lessons
learning_outcomes: list the fruit of the Holy Spirit as guided in Galatians 5:22-23
describe how they apply the fruit of the Holy Spirit in their lives
desire to be led by the Holy Spirit in their daily activities.
learning_experiences: in pairs read Galatians 5: 22-23
list the fruit of the Holy Spirit; love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, humility, self-control
write the fruit of the Holy Spirit on flash cards and display it in class
in groups list good things, they should do to others as Christians
discuss how they apply the fruit of the Holy Spirit in daily lives
compose and sing a song on the fruit of the Holy Spirit.
Suggested Learning Experiences
inquiry_questions: Why should you have the fruit of the Holy Spirit?
Key Inquiry Question(s)
core_competencies: • Creativity and imagination: the skill of originality is nurtured as learners compose a song on the fruit of the Holy Spirit.
values: • Peace is exhibited as learners practise the fruit of the Holy spirit that is-peace and live peacefully with others.
pertinent_issues: • Peace Education is enhanced as learners list good things they should do to others as Christians.
links_to_other_areas: English: reading skills are enhanced as learners read the Holy Bible.
Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners compose and sing a songs.

substrands.name: Self-control 2 lessons
learning_outcomes: practice self-control as guided in Galatians 5:23-25
make right decisions that are guided by the Holy Spirit
demonstrate self-control by avoiding behaviour that defiles the body
Desire to live Godly lives guided by the Holy Spirit.
learning_experiences: read Galatians 5:23-25
role play,’ making decisions that portray self-control’
in groups list choices they make in their day-to-day lives
list things that can defile them e.g. engaging in sex, watching ungodly movies, drug use and abuse
say how they can avoid defiling their bodies
compose a song on self-control: Galatians 5:23-25.
inquiry_questions: Why should you have self-control?
core_competencies: Learning to learn: the skill of working collaboratively is portrayed as learners list choices they make in their day-to-day lives.
Imagination and creativity: the skill of originality is exhibited as learners role play,’ making decisions that portray self-control.’
Core competencies to be developed:
Communication: listening skills are enhanced as learners use social media devices to listen to a gospel song or watch a video clip based on the Bible. Pertinent and contemporary Issues:
Patriotism: learners show responsibility by using social media responsibly. Values
Responsibility: learners use social media responsibly.
Integrity: learners use social media well even when no one is watching them. Link to other learning areas:
Science and technology skills are applied as learners manipulate digital devices.
